headline: Measles-related deaths reach 867 in Bangladesh; 4 more die in 24 hours
summary: Four more individuals have died from measles or measles-like symptoms in the last 24 hours, bringing the total confirmed and suspected death toll this year to 867. The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) also reported 677 new suspected cases.
details: Bangladesh has recorded 867 confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths this year, with four additional fatalities reported in the last 24 hours until yesterday morning. This ongoing health crisis continues to affect communities nationwide.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), two of the latest deaths were confirmed as measles-related, while the other two were suspected cases. This brings the confirmed death toll to 98 and suspected deaths to 769.

In the same 24-hour period, 677 new suspected measles cases were reported, raising the nationwide tally to 135,332. Additionally, 99 laboratory-confirmed cases were identified, increasing the total confirmed infections to 17,040.
Since March 15, a significant 117,444 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country. Of these, 113,200 individuals have successfully recovered, as per DGHS data.

headline_marked: [[PM visits Matarbari deep-sea port]] in Cox's Bazar, inspects flood-hit areas in Chittagong
headline: PM visits Matarbari deep-sea port in Cox's Bazar, inspects flood-hit areas in Chittagong
summary: The Prime Minister will inspect the Matarbari deep-sea port and coal-fired power project, marking her first visit to Chittagong since taking office in February. She will also assess flood damage and attend rehabilitation programs.
details: The Prime Minister is undertaking a significant visit to Chittagong and Cox's Bazar today. This marks her first trip to the Chittagong region since assuming office in February.

Her itinerary begins in the morning with a helicopter journey from Dhaka to Matarbari in Maheshkhali Upazila, Cox's Bazar. There, she will inspect the Matarbari deep-sea port, the coal-fired power project, and the activities of the Maheshkhali Integrated Development Authority (MIDA).

Following this, the Prime Minister will participate in a program at Paschim Banshkhali High School and College field in Baharchhara Union. This event is organized for the rehabilitation of those affected by recent floods.

In the afternoon, she will visit Al-Jamiyatul Islamia Azizul Ulum Babunagar Madrasa in Fatikchhari, Chittagong. She is scheduled to meet with Allama Shah Muhibbullah Babunagari and later visit the grave of the late Allama Shah Ahmad Shafi.

Later in the afternoon, the Prime Minister will take a break at the Hathazari District Council Dak Bungalow. Afterwards, she is expected to attend another flood rehabilitation program at Hathazari Government College field.
The day will conclude with her participation in an organizational meeting at the Radisson Blu Hotel in Chittagong in the evening. The Prime Minister will then depart for Dhaka later tonight.
